items.title: WHO launches working papers on traditional medicine
items.summary: The WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre is launching a series of working papers designed to document and examine traditional, complementary and integrative medicine (TCIM) worldwide. The inaugural publication, Cupping therapy: descriptive synthesis of training, provides a first-of-its-kind overview of training approaches for cupping therapy primarily based on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). items.title: WHO and ENHYPEN join efforts to inspire young blood donors globally
items.summary: World Health Organization (WHO) Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus met with global K-pop group ENHYPEN in Seoul on 22 October to celebrate the success of their collaboration for World Blood Donor Day 2026 and recognize the group's role in inspiring young people around the world to donate blood and save lives.

items.title: New global framework launched to track increasing health risks of extreme heat for pregnant women, newborns and children
items.summary: As extreme heat intensifies around the world, the World Health Organization (WHO), the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), UNICEF and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) today launched the first-ever set of priority indicators to help countries track the health impacts of heat on pregnant women, newborns and children.

items.title: WHO launches guidance on evidence generation for new TB diagnostics
items.summary: WHO has published new Guidance on evidence generation (GEG) for new tuberculosis diagnostics. This guidance informs researchers, developers, funders and other stakeholders about how evidence should be generated to optimally inform WHO guideline development on new TB diagnostic tests, sample types and testing strategies.

items.title: New WHO–ILO framework to track progress towards universal social protection inclusive of people with TB
items.summary: WHO and ILO have published a new monitoring and evaluation framework to enable countries to track progress towards universal social protection inclusive of people with tuberculosis (TB). The new framework provides a practical approach to measuring progress towards the commitment to ensure that 100% of people with TB have access to a health and social benefits package by 2027, and identifying gaps in coverage and protection.

items.title: WHO report examines inequalities in noncommunicable diseases and their risk factors
items.summary: The State of inequality: noncommunicable diseases and their risk factors report published today by the World Health Organization (WHO) provides a global assessment of inequalities in noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and their risk factors, examining differences between population groups within countries. items.summary: Rewatch the event Conversation on traditional medicine continued this year at the World Health Summit (WHS) 2026 in Berlin. This marked the third event at the WHS since 2025, in which a dedicated session explored the challenges and opportunities of traditional medicine in advancing global health goals. items.title: WHO releases training manual to expand access to early breast cancer care
items.summary: WHO has published the Global Breast Cancer Initiative (GBCI) Training Manual – a package for programme managers. This technical derivative product of the WHO Global Breast Cancer Initiative implementation framework provides guidance to countries establishing or strengthening their breast cancer programmes.

items.title: WHO and ADVANCE-ID strengthen clinical trial capacity through workshop
items.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Advancing Clinical Evidence in Infectious Diseases (ADVANCE-ID) Network jointly organised the ADVANCE-ID Clinical Trial Workshop 2026, held from 31 August to 2 September 2026 in Singapore. The workshop contributed to wider capacity-strengthening efforts through the Global Clinical Trials Forum (GCTF), bringing together researchers from different regions to strengthen practical skills in the design and conduct of high-quality clinical trials.ADVANCE-ID

items.title: Early menopause: Why better research and global guidance matter for women’s health
items.summary: Physician and scientist Priya Satalkar-Götz experienced her first symptoms of menopause in her mid-twenties, but it took several years for her to receive a diagnosis. items.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus - Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Between 1 January and 5 October 2026, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reported eight laboratory-confirmed cases of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection, including one death. Cases were detected across six locations: Al Jouf (1), Arar (1), Hafr Al-Batin (1), Riyadh (2), Tabuk (1) and Taif (2). No epidemiological links were identified between any of the cases. According to these reports, the individual died on 2 October following hospitalization for severe pneumonia on 29 September, and pneumonic plague was suspected as the cause of death, following occupational exposure in laboratory settings. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: On 5 October 2026, WHO was informed about a laboratory-confirmed imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Kenya with travel history from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The patient travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Kenya through Uganda. The patient was hospitalized and treated in Kenya but subsequently died on 5 October. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 11 September 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded further, with two additional health zones affected. These include Bulu health zone in a new province, Sud Ubangi, located on the north-west part of the country and Dungu health zone in Haut-Uélé province, bordering South Sudan. items.summary: Since the last Disease Outbreak News was published on 28 August 2026, the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded to one additional health zone, Kayna, in North Kivu. This increase brings the total number of affected health zones to 61 across six out of 26 provinces of the country: Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is in a phase of intense transmission. It is the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the country and expanding faster than any previous Ebola outbreak. The epidemic is increasingly characterized by sustained transmission within interconnected geographic clusters. items.title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is intensifying, with sustained transmission and continued increases in reported cases and deaths. items.summary: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains active, with sustained transmission driving increases in reported cases and deaths.
